Long Version:
My computer for comparison:
GIGABYTE Windforce edition of NVIDIA GTX 1070 with all drivers updated before a single minute of play
Intel I7-3770
16GB of RAM
Win 7 64-bit
960GB SSD by Samsung
I'll keep this as concise as I can but bear with me as I like to provide detail.
Gameplay: Everything is clunky when it comes to interacting with the world. Everything stutters and if it doesnt then the game is probably about to stall off and on for the next minute. I could that my graphics card and processor were not having any issues mainly because up until running into these stalls I was getting around 60FPS. Rendering, AI detection, and occasionally pathing are all so messed up its just plain sad. Spiders, hyenas, etc spawn right on top of me fairly often when roaming around, cant figure out how to run around the sharp angle of a cliff to get to the way up, or don't even bother being loaded until you are with a few arms lengths from them. And more often then not, when NPCs do spawn in they do one of four things: glide around without moving a muscle from their pose, are stuck five feet up in the air and can't move just turn, sit there on their bedroll and just look at me until their buddy half a football field away notices me and comes gliding over to attack, OR they are spawn halfway into the ground and can not do a flipping thing about it. Animals, at least, manage to spawn most of the time above ground and don't understand how to traverse terrain....often hardly at all.
There is little to know group mentalities for animals where it should be present. Prime example, when I attack one gazalle there other just stands there or walks around like he/she didn't see nothing. But if I attack one Hyena the packs from all the surrounding zip codes hear about it and come running to help or just decide to spawn/teleport right next to the fight.
You can clear a cave or area in a couple minutes and the mobs will respawn within minutes or more often than not in seconds. I ventured into a spider cave while in God mode thinking I could kill the spawn or smash their eggs to see less of them for awhile or God forbid finding their mother and killing her. I hate super large spiders, especially when there is no flamethrower nearby. I found that there was neither a flamethrower, nor anything I could do to slow their spawning.
Any interaction with NPCs is no different from killing endless hyena packs other than the hyenas spawn a little faster. Also during the combat you can be disarmed, or knocked down, repeatedly, endlessly, until you die there is little to no counter to such onslaughts.
Building and smithing are both interesting and somewhat fun aspects of the game but there is no map of the controls, nor help with them. Furthermore, resources can be scarce and with how hostile the map is already it is very difficult to make into the mid-tier let alone end/late game areas. More to come on this area...
Ranged combat, I found it to often be negligible as enemies would take 3 and 7 arrows to die or be within a couple punches of death. Yes I had points into the skill tree to increase the damage output. Which eventually made archery at least decent. That is until I went to retrieve any arrow..because once you fire it, it can never come back. Missed and hit a tree? Nope you can't get that one either. Hit the sand between your feet? Nope, that arrow is irretrievable too. Javelins and bolts included in this as well. Though the positive here is that there are many times of both arrows and bolts for your bow or crossbow. Javelins can be used a polearm or thrown your choice which is great.
There are fish but there is no giant man-eater in the water, at least not yet. (Referring to one of the above screenshots on the store-page.)
Combat, melee combat, can be utter garbage with animations and my character literally standing there not-responding. They were disarmed, stunned, crippled, thrown by a two-handed hammer, or any such thing, it was a classic light hit and I had almost full stamina and the character just stands there holding my sword but not doing a dang thing before I can even rectify this the enemy has killed me.
Graphics and Audio:
The game looks great, and sounds great, when its not rendering something. Otherwise it is very bland. Though Audio all around is just magnificent in some regards I'd say the audio is just a bit above Skyrim's at release back in 2011. I'm being sincere, kudos, pat on the back and take a day off whoever did the audio for this thus far. Just that one person in the audio department.....not the whole development team...the rest of y'all got a lot of work to do. I really don't even want to know what that little man thing with two eyes and thin arms is but for goodness sake does he even have a proper detailed mesh and texture? Its a hideous blob that chances me around the map and I don't even understand what the heck it is. And even after I killed one in a couple hits with my stone sword it was completely unrecognizable even when his "face" was rendered. I understand its probably not meant to be the next version of an old man Ken barbie doll but dang he makes Ryan Reynolds' Deadpool look like a super model, yes without both masks.
Bug Fixing and Optimizations: I know I've bashed the game a lot by this point. But here goes....
Weapon stuck in hand post-combat. I understand that you can run around around with your weapons out. BUT this instance I was trying to run normally with no weapons equipped. The animation was correct, aside from the weapon in my hand, and my character as though the weapon was not there but visibly it was. I could even fist fight while my axe was in my hand.
Mobs/animals/humans spawning halfway or partially in the terrain. This happened all over the place, spiders would spawn on top of the ceiling and somehow fall through or in the walls, etc.
No harvest bug. This is a classic issue that I saw also in my time playing ARK: Survival Evolved and it looks like it is in this game too. I resovled this issue by harvesting something completely different than what node had fallen asleep and then left the area and came back. The node/individual plants and trees that were not harvestable were harvestable again.
Vegetation can reseed...inside your house and has no qualms about spawning right out side your front door. This has happened many times.
You can punch water? While swimming? Also no surface swimming but I can jump in the middle of any deep water. I can get some air by jumping in deep water while swimming....correct me if I'm wrong but isn't that supposed to not be possible? Also, either everyone is Jesus and knows how to walk on water or no one knows how to swim at all--these are the two ai protocols that everything but an alligator has when it comes deep water and swimming.
More to come but I've hit my limit and will update this...

Crysis Warhead is a direct stand-alone sub-sequel to the first Crysis game. You change characters in this game to the cliched "edge-lord baddass wannabe" Psycho (actual callsign) from the first game. It's a rather unmemorable side-quest of sorts while the original main character Nomad from the first game does his own thing elsewhere. As this game uses assets and functionallity from the first I'll just C&P those details from my review of the first game here:
Contrary to popular belief Crysis doesn't really stand the test of time for gameplay. As an FPS it's solid but mediocre mechanically with heavy restrictions imposed by the MMS generation of FPS. Ways it still excells are the fast paced combat with impactful gunplay, and a great sense of tactical variety. The primary negatives stem from the rather poorly implimented suit mechanics and limited weapon sets. You can carry a wide variety of weapons sure, but the ammo between them is not universal where it should be forcing you to keep a common weapon in one of your two main slots - both should be common if you want to be efficient - and one set of pistols (akimbo), knife for melee, and a rocket launcher or other "special" weapon. The only way to circumvent this limitation is console commands. Thing about realism in games is that it's often worse than the mechanical advantages of the fantasies we've had in games prior. If you're going to intentionally limit your mechanics compared to past examples then you must offer a benefit of some kind to offset that discrepency rather than hiding behind the "realism" excuse. It just felt artificially handicapping. Why couldn't I swap out the rarely used rocket launcher for a 3rd main? Why can't Strength, Speed, and Armor all auto-swap as needed? Even Cloak can be auto-swapped too, but that should be optional. As the suit controls stand you have to manually activate the mode appropriate to the action before using the action like Strength before punching or grabbing and throwing, and Speed before Sprinting. Instead these functions could've been auto-swapped on use but otherwise defaulting to Speed until struck and switching to Armor. Movement speed is a bit sluggish for my taste without the Speed mode.
Graphically it's still a work of art. It still chugs and brings even modern graphics cards to their knees at 4K, but only because it's not fully optimized and DX10. Current mid-range graphics cards will get a solid 60+ at 1080p near max settings. Some settings though such as DoF and FoV are obfuscated into console commands (IIRC). Personally played it on an R9 290 at 1440p near max settings and it was a smooth ~55 for me. I would love a modern CryEngine HD remaster of the game; it would look sharper and run smoother.
And that concludes the C&P. Like I was saying about the story though, and it is skippable, is that you go on little more than an inconsequential side-quest as the side character Psycho from the prior game. The story is heavily referencial to his past to generate a lore and background for him and his attitude; all of which is very contrived and cliched.
The world design takes a bit of a stumble leaning more heavily on linear pathing with little opportunity for varied tactics. Let me make this perfectly clear though as I'm being rather harsh; It's a good game and I do recommend it, but it does not hold its own to the original in any way. It's worthwhile in its own right.

There are many Pro's but sadly some Con's, Just for warning's before you buy it.
Pro's:
- Dramatic Story
- Good Graphic's
-Fun to play
- Being able to import avatar from ME1
- NPC Conversations can interesting
- Combat is pretty good in my point of view
But yeah, I'll always play this game and I really hope others will enjoy it as much as I do.

Con's:
-Some glitch's here and there
-When every avatar turn's into black pixel's (It's happened in the first one too.)
-Sometimes subtiles are highlighted black (Dont know if that's done for a reason)

I had previously left a positive review for this game, but the ever inflating price of DLC is a joke. This game was complete two years ago, it lives on only as a cash cow for Paradox. As a company, Paradox is setting a legendarily low bar for DLC in terms of price, frequency and lack of content. Don't buy this game. Don't send Paradox a message that it can get away with its money-grubbing and lack of innovation.
